changes: Columnar top-k always admits physical execution scratch and retains an owned selected batch. Borrowed candidates detach before scanner advance; owned candidates retain their existing backing.
Remove duplicate unowned merge and output branches, using owned concatenation, top-k and row materialization for both scanner capabilities.
Enable explicit owned results for borrowed column scanners.
Normalize ordering through the existing scoped normalization helper, releasing planning storage at query completion.

new_boundary_cases: Plain and owned results preserve binary winners across two reused borrowed batches.
Exact observed allocation peak succeeds; one byte below rejects; success and failure release query reservations.
validation.http_routes: Borrowed eager baseline explicitly asserts scanColumns execution; range-honoring deferred route still asserts rank-only then winner-only reads. Four concurrent cold/warm jobs at 64/128 MiB and read cap two.

remaining: Caller/borrowed scanner source allocations remain outside admission; this covers retained candidate data and supported execution workspaces.
Selected physical views can reference larger dictionaries; detachment charges the physical backing it copies, not just logical selected rows.
Other planner/decoder/runtime allocations and whole-Worker heap limits remain open.
Earlier HTTP metrics are historical; the current borrowed adapter now exposes scanColumns as well as scanVectorBatches.
